## Summary

`skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` scoped-lint path hands the raw git changed-file list to eslint without an extension filter. When the changed-file list contains a Python file (.py), eslint v6.4.0 parses it as JavaScript and emits a fatal "Parsing error: Unterminated string constant" — surfaced as a blocking high-severity finding that fails audits closed (Phase 1 decision gate), even though the flagged file is valid Python and unrelated to the item under audit.

discovered-from:SA-0MSKM2LSP006L0K8

## Root cause

- `_run_eslint_findings_check` (`skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py:351`): `cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]` — passes raw `files` with no extension filter.
- `_run_eslint_fix_mode` (`:722`, `:727`): same gap.
- By contrast, ruff scoping filters to Python extensions: `py_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith((".py", ".pyi", ".pyx"))]` (`:392`, `:641`).
- Consequence (observed 2026-09-20): audit of SA-0MSKM2LSP006L0K8 returned "Ready to close: No" because an unrelated uncommitted `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` modification entered the changed-file scope and eslint mis-parsed it, demoting a previously completed/in_review item to open/plan_complete.

## Reproduction (read-only)

eslint skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py -f json --quiet  -> fatal "Parsing error: Unterminated string constant" (1:3)
eslint skill/audit/scripts/scan.py -f json --quiet             -> identical error (unrelated committed .py)
eslint tests/node/<any>.mjs -f json --quiet                    -> [] (clean)
python3 -m py_compile skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py -> OK (valid Python)

Same class of bug as CG-0MSXL2L0T009CA3I (ruff mis-parsing .ts files, 627 false positives) — fixed for ruff but not for eslint.

## Suggested fix

- Filter the scoped `files` list in `_run_eslint_findings_check` / `_run_eslint_fix_mode` to JS/TS extensions (.js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .tsx) before building the eslint command; skip eslint entirely (return []) when no JS/TS targets remain — mirror the ruff guard.
- Whole-project mode (empty/absent files list) already avoids the issue: `eslint <root>` with no explicit targets only lints default JS extensions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scoped eslint runs filter file targets to JS/TS extensions; a .py-only changed-file list produces zero eslint findings (eslint skipped or given no JS/TS targets).
- [ ] Unit test asserts no eslint invocation / no findings when the scoped file list contains only non-JS/TS files.
- [ ] An audit whose changed-file scope contains only .py files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding (regression).

# Browser suite contention: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` lets two full suites starve each other

Discovered while auditing TCE `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — `discovered-from:CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I`.

## Problem
`run_tests.py` bounds concurrent test runs with `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default **2**, introduced by `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG`). Two concurrent full suites — e.g. two `implement.py finish` gates in different TCE worktrees, plus an audit's F3 auto-execution — each spin up a 4-worker Chromium browser stage (`maxWorkers: 4` in `vite.config.ts`). On a single host this oversubscribes CPU/GPU, so timing-sensitive browser tests time out and vitest runs get **SIGKILLed (exit 137)** or **hang (exit 124)**.

## Impact
A repo can go many hours without a green full-suite run, blocking audits/releases and producing misleading `test-failure` items.

**TCE evidence (2026-09-20):** last green full-suite cache entry **~29 h old**; consecutive entries `exit 124 / 137 / 1 / 1`; observed **≥2 concurrent full suites** and **30+ vitest/chromium processes**; load average ~8–12 on 16 cores. `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` fails 3 animation-timeout tests under load while passing **6/6 in isolation** (10.2 s).

## Expected Behaviour
- Full-suite runs (or at least browser-heavy suites) are serialized per repo/host to **1**.
- `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` becomes context-aware (browser suites ⇒ 1) or the default drops where a Chromium stage is present.
- `implement.py` full-suite gates acquire the guard and log `queued_at` / `wait_seconds` rather than colliding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two full project suites in the same repo never execute their browser stages simultaneously (verified by observing serialized runs / semaphore telemetry).
- [ ] `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (or a browser-stage-specific cap) prevents cross-suite browser starvation; the behaviour is documented.
- [ ] `implement.py` full-suite gates acquire the guard and emit a `queued_at`/`wait_seconds` log line.
- [ ] A TCE full-suite re-run during a multi-agent period yields a green full-suite cache entry.

## Related Work
- `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG` — Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive (the `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` default of 2 this refines).
- `CG-0MUA7RRXL007GEHW` (TCE) — the timing-fragile `upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` surfaced by this contention.
- `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (TCE) — audit blocked on obtaining a green full-suite run.

## Key Files
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` handling.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` / `skill/shared/queue.py` — shared bounded-concurrency primitive.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the full-suite finish gate.

# Report renderer reports Children: 0 for parents with children

## Summary

The shared report helper `scripts/render_report.py` (skills/report) fetches work-item data with `wl show <id> --json` and reads the children count from that payload. Because `wl show <id> --json` (without `--children`) does not include the children array, the count is always zero and the canonical end-of-session report renders `Children: 👥 0` even when the item has many children. The report skill's own spec states the Children field source is the `children` array length from `wl show <id> --children --json`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a work item with at least one child.
2. Run `python3 $(skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py <id> --skill-name plan --headline "..."`.
3. Observe `- **Children:** 👥 0` in the Meta-Data block, even though `wl show <id> --children --json` returns the children.

Concrete example: AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292 has 11 children at stage `plan_complete`, yet the report rendered on 2026-09-20 shows `Children: 👥 0`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `render_report.py` fetches children via `wl show <id> --children --json` (or otherwise reads the top-level `children` array) when populating the Meta-Data Children count.
- The rendered report shows the real child count for a parent with children (at least 11 for the example above).
- Behaviour for leaf items (no children) remains `Children: 👥 0`.
- Existing report tests pass (updated if they encoded the wrong payload shape).

## Notes

- discovered-from:AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292 (a plan run exposed the issue; the report was pasted verbatim per the skill so the incorrect count was surfaced to the operator rather than silently corrected).
- File: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py` (line ~383 `cmd = ["wl", "show", work_item_id, "--json"]`; line ~232 `metadata["Children"] = ...`).
- Spec reference: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/SKILL.md` — "Children | `children` array length".
- Agent infrastructure (`.pi/agent/skills`) — not edited inline per repository-boundary rules.
- Related precedent: AH-0MTFRZQLN007IV0E (tree_coverage read children from the wrong JSON key).

## Auto-Plan Decision

- **Effort:** Extra Small
- **Risk:** Low (score: 0)
- **Decision:** Proceed to implement (effort and risk below threshold)

## Automated Review Summary

1. **Requirements & AC alignment:** ACs faithfully match the bug report; each traces to a specific fix point. No gaps.
2. **Completeness:** Description, ACs, file paths, spec reference all present and valid.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies:** No children or dependency edges; no-op.
4. **Scope sizing:** No children; no-op. Bug is a single-line fix.
5. **Acceptance & testability:** All four ACs are clear, measurable, testable.
6. **Polish & handoff:** Well-formatted with reproduction steps, concrete example, file references.

### Recommended Fix

Add `--children` to the `wl show` command in `render_from_wl()` (line ~384 of `scripts/render_report.py`):

```python
cmd = ["wl", "show", work_item_id, "--children", "--json"]
```

data.description:
The end-of-session report helper (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) always renders **Audit: ❔ not run** in the Meta-Data block, even when the work item has a persisted, passing audit.

### Root cause

`wl show <id> --json` returns `auditResult` as a **top-level** key of the response envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "workItem": { ... }, "auditResult": { "readyToClose": true, ... }, "comments": [...] }
```

`render_metadata()` reads `work_item.get("auditResult")` (line ~235), where `work_item = data.get("workItem", {})` — the top-level `auditResult` is never consulted, so the lookup is always falsy and the audit status degrades to "not run".

Discovered while rendering the final report for SA-0MU7FD0YF0065EG9, whose audit had passed (`readyToClose: true`, all 4 ACs met) yet the report showed "Audit: not run".

### Acceptance Criteria

1. `render_metadata()` resolves audit status from the top-level `auditResult` of the `wl show --json` envelope (falling back to any `workItem.auditResult` for backward compatibility), so a `readyToClose: true` result renders as passed and `readyToClose: false` renders as failed.
2. A unit test covers: top-level `auditResult` with `readyToClose: true` → "passed"; `readyToClose: false` → "failed"; absent/null → "not run".
3. `--json` (stdin) mode continues to work for callers that pass a bare work-item dict.

---

# Fix inherited_pass bypass: three fixes in audit_runner.py

## Summary
The audit runner incorrectly allows `inherited_pass` to bypass the pre-review stage block, producing false-positive "Ready to close: Yes" verdicts. This task combines three related fixes in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Fix 1: inherited_pass assignment (line ~9897)

In the `if not parent_gaps:` branch, add a stage guard so `inherited_pass=True` is only applied to children already in `in_review` or `done` stage. Pre-review children (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) must not receive `inherited_pass` — they must be audited independently.

- Code at ~9897 checks child stage before setting `inherited_pass = True`
- Only children with `stage` in `("in_review", "done")` receive `inherited_pass`
- Pre-review stage children skip the `inherited_pass` branch and proceed to independent audit
- Existing `_child_content_changed` guard is preserved

## Fix 2: all_children_reviewed check (line ~4207)

The `all_children_reviewed` check currently allows `inherited_pass` to exempt a child from the stage check:

```python
all_children_reviewed = all(
    c.get("stage") in ("in_review", "done") or c.get("inherited_pass")
    for c in active_children
)
```

Remove `or c.get("inherited_pass")` — the stage check should be independent. The `inherited_pass` flag affects the verdict, not the stage blocking logic.

- `all_children_reviewed` only checks child stages, not `inherited_pass`
- A child at `intake_complete` with `inherited_pass=True` is correctly counted as blocking
- Existing exempt-child logic (deleted, completed/done) is preserved

## Fix 3: summary text (line ~4333)

The summary unconditionally appends "All children are in in_review or done stage." when `all_children_reviewed` is true. Fix this so the line is only emitted when that statement is actually true; otherwise, the summary names the blocking children.

- The "All children are in in_review or done stage." line is only emitted when all active children are actually in those stages
- When children block closure, the summary names them
- No regression on existing "Ready to close: No" cases that already name blocking children

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three fixes applied in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- [ ] Regression test passes (separate task SA-0MUD5OMQG0068P4I)
- [ ] No regression on existing tests

- [ ] Existing exempt-child logic preserved

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~4201-4214, ~4330-4340, ~9890-9910)

# Intake: Audit-runner pi calls crash with `Connection error.` from stale-ctx extension exceptions

## Problem statement

Audit-runner `pi` subprocesses crash mid-call and the runner records
`provider_error: Connection error.` because pi extensions loaded into the audit
session throw on a **stale `ExtensionContext`** after pi replaces or reloads the
session. The **fatal uncaught exception** is thrown by the ContextHub-owned
`worklog` recovery extension (`register-recovery.ts`, `_notifyFn` →
`ctx.ui.notify`), not by `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. Two
SorraAgents-owned extensions (`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals`)
throw the *same* stale-ctx error but pi catches those and prints them as
(non-fatal) `Extension error (...)` lines. This blocks audits and therefore the
ship final-validation gate (exit 12).

## Users

- **Release manager** — needs audits to complete so `dev` → `main` is not blocked
  by spurious provider failures.
  - *As a release manager, I want an audit pi call to return a genuine verdict
    even after an extension-triggered session replacement, so the release gate
    is not blocked by an infrastructure crash.*
- **Audit operator** — needs `provider_error` entries in the debug corpus to
  reflect real provider faults, not extension crashes.
  - *As an audit operator, I want the audit debug log to distinguish a real
    provider fault from an extension exception, so I can triage correctly.*
- **Pi extension maintainer** — needs extensions to fail safe when the session
  they were registered against is replaced.
  - *As a maintainer, I want my extension's async callbacks to no-op when the
    captured ctx is invalid, so a session swap cannot crash an unrelated run.*

## Existing state (evidence)

The failure was captured for the audit of **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** (now deleted).
The debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
(`context=parent`) records:

- `reason: provider_error`, `provider_error: "Connection error."`,
  `elapsed_seconds: ~713`.
- `raw_stderr` contains one `Extension error
  (/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts): This
  extension ctx is stale ...` line, one identical line for
  `proxy-sse-signals`, and then the **fatal, uncaught** trace:

  ```
  Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. ...
      at ExtensionRunner.assertActive (...)
      at get ui (...)
      at _notifyFn (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts:71:41)
      at _notifyRetryAttempt (.../register-recovery.ts:549:5)
      at triggerInvisibleContinue (.../register-recovery.ts:391:7)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (...)
  Node.js v22.22.1
  ```

  The trailing `Node.js v22.22.1` banner shows the pi process **crashed**; the
  audit runner then surfaced `Connection error.` from the pi JSON stream.

Corpus scan across every `reason=provider_error` entry
(`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl`) shows **all** non-empty
`raw_stderr` provider errors carry the `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx stack;
some also carry the `proxy-compaction-bridge` / `proxy-sse-signals`
`Extension error` lines (non-fatal, caught by pi).

Root cause of each stale access:

- `ContextHub .../register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` is assigned a closure over
  the *handler's* `ctx` (`_notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(...)`,
  lines ~84/87/212) and is later invoked from the async retry loop
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`). If the session was replaced/reloaded in
  between, `ctx.ui` throws — and because the call originates in a timer/async
  callback, pi never catches it and the process dies.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — both `after_provider_response`
  and `context` handlers call `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` on the event
  ctx; a stale ctx throws.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — `turn_start` captures `ctx.ui` as
  `statusUi`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls `statusUi.setStatus(...)`
  on the stale UI handle.

`pi` supports `--no-extensions` / `-ne` (disables extension discovery), alongside
the `--no-context-files --no-skills` flags the audit runner already adds to
`_call_pi`. Audit prompts are read-only and fully self-contained, so they do not
depend on extensions.

## Desired change

1. **Unblock audit calls (SorraAgents-owned):** stop loading interactive/UI
   extensions in audit-runner pi subprocesses — add `--no-extensions` to the
   `_call_pi` command (mirroring the existing context-reduction flags).
2. **Harden the SorraAgents-owned extensions:** make `proxy-compaction-bridge`
   and `proxy-sse-signals` fail safe on a stale/replaced ctx — never call
   `ctx.ui`/`ctx.sessionManager` on an invalidated ctx (guard, re-capture from a
   fresh handler, or no-op/passthrough).
3. **Fatal crash (cross-repo handoff — delivered):** the ContextHub
   `worklog` recovery-extension stale-ctx crash is handed off to
   **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (`Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale
   ExtensionContext after session replacement (_notifyFn)`), which is not edited
   from this SorraAgents work item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No extension crash on audit calls:** the audit runner's `_call_pi` command
   excludes extension discovery (`--no-extensions`). Verified by a unit test
   asserting the constructed command (both tool-enabled and tool-disabled paths).
2. **Stale-ctx-safe SorraAgents extensions:** `proxy-compaction-bridge` and
   `proxy-sse-signals` no-op (context passthrough / status unchanged) when their
   handler or async callback observes an invalidated `ctx`, never throwing.
   Verified by `node:test` unit tests injecting a stale-ctx stub.
3. **Re-audit completes genuinely:** a re-audit of SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB (or an
   equivalent audit pi call that triggers a session replacement) completes with a
   genuine verdict (`met`/`partial`/`adjusted`) and the debug entry's `reason` is
   not `provider_error` with `Connection error.` attributable to an extension
   exception.
4. **Regression tests:** a stale/replaced-session-ctx regression test exists for
   both `pi-client` extensions (Node unit tests) and a Python test asserts the
   audit `_call_pi` command includes `--no-extensions`; the tests fail against
   the pre-fix code.
5. **Docs + full suite:** `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` (F6) are updated to reflect the corrected
   attribution/fix; all related documentation (code comments, README, docs) is
   updated; and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo boundary:** the fatal crash is in
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` (separate repo and `WL-` worklog). It is
  **not** edited from this item; the fix is tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B.
- **Do not regress** the compaction-bridge wire contract
  (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) or the dispatch reshape semantics/tests.
- **Do not weaken fail-closed audit behaviour**; the audit runner must still
  return `unmet`/`partial` on genuine provider errors, not mask them.
- `--no-extensions` affects all discovered extensions in audit calls only; the
  interactive TUI extension behaviour (compaction mirroring, status line,
  recovery) must remain unchanged.
- `wl`-tracked, test-first, build → test → commit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi` builds the pi command
  (~L3648); add `--no-extensions`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — command-flag tests (~L267–304);
  add the `--no-extensions` assertion.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — guard/re-bind the session id
  used by `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js` — pure core (no ctx
  access); keep behaviour, extend tests only.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — guard the captured `statusUi` used by
  the capturing-fetch callback.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
  `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` — stale-ctx regression coverage.
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`, `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` —
  documentation/correction.
- *(cross-repo, tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B)*
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`.

## Related work (manual)

- **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** — `[test-failure] getCompletedOrInReviewItems ...`
  (`discovered-from`; the audit that failed with this signature; now deleted).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for
  child audits in the final-validation gate (records the same failure as the
  motivation for removing manual interruptions).
- **SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL** — RCA: Audit Pipeline Reliability
  (`docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`); F6 documents the 9 `provider_error`
  entries (incl. `Connection error.`) and their conflation with parse failures.
- **SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0** — origin of `proxy-compaction-bridge` (wire contract
  LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- **SA-0MSHAKSEA001LQ6T** — origin of `proxy-sse-signals`.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — audit context reduction
  (`--no-context-files --no-skills`); precedent for adding a loader flag to
  `_call_pi`.
- **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (ContextHub) — handoff item for the fatal
  `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/cross-repo).** Debug-log evidence shows the *fatal* uncaught
  exception is thrown by the ContextHub-owned `worklog` extension
  (`register-recovery.ts`), not `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. How should
  this item be scoped?
  - Answer (producer): **(c) analysis/handoff** — do not edit ContextHub from this
    item; **create a `WL-` item** for the fatal `register-recovery` crash, and do
    the SorraAgents-side extensions/audit fixes + tests here.
  - Evidence: created **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** in ContextHub; SorraAgents-side
    work captured in the ACs above (consistent with Q3 = (a), which names tests
    for the `pi-client` extensions and the audit `--no-extensions` command).
- **Q2 (audit extension policy).** Is disabling extension discovery for
  audit-runner pi calls (`pi ... --no-extensions`, alongside
  `--no-context-files --no-skills`) acceptable?
  - Answer (producer): **n/a** — not separately decided; Q3(a) explicitly names
    the `--no-extensions` command assertion, so it is in scope (AC1/AC4).
- **Q3 (regression-test surface).** Where should the stale-ctx regression test
  live?
  - Answer (producer): **(a)** Node unit tests for both `pi-client` extensions
    plus a Python test asserting the audit pi command includes `--no-extensions`.
  - Recorded as AC4.

## Problem Statement

Agents repeatedly make the same mistakes when working with pi — using `skill_path` as a bash command instead of the tool, expanding backticks in shell commands, forgetting Python imports, and falling into self-correction loops. A skill that analyses recent session logs to detect these patterns would enable proactive skill improvements and prevent recurring failures.

## Users

- **Agent operator / PI** — receives a structured report of agent confusion patterns and actionable improvement recommendations.
- **Skill authors** — get targeted work items to update SKILL.md files, scripts, or add guardrails.
- **Producers** — understand systemic agent behaviour issues across the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill reads the last 20 session logs (`.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl`) for the CWD project, sorted by modification time.
2. Heuristic analysis extracts: tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals (keywords: error, fail, retry, incorrect, sorry, wrong, fix, correct, issue, problem, confused, wait, actually, oh, hmm, ah), tool result errors (tracebacks, permission denied, command not found, shell expansion errors), and retry/self-correction patterns.
3. LLM-assisted interpretation (via pi calls) classifies patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generates recommendations.
4. Structured report rendered in the agent response with: summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations (which sessions showed which patterns).
5. Recommendations are filed as worklog comments on the parent work item.
6. For each actionable recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, and linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description.
7. The skill follows existing project conventions: `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/`, `skill/agent-log-review/tests/`.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics for extraction, LLM for classification — not fully automated LLM-only (too expensive) and not heuristic-only (too noisy).
- Only CWD project sessions; no cross-project analysis.
- Auto-create work items but don't implement them — that's downstream work.
- Must handle v3 session log format (session, model_change, thinking_level_change, message types with content as list of thinking/toolCall parts).

## Existing State

- Session logs exist at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` in v3 format.
- Existing skills follow `SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `tests/` convention.
- Related work: SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 (tag pi sessions spawned from skills with `--session-id`), SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD (24h experiment: measure session length & token use), SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA and reliability recommendations for audit failures), SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH (Add 'waiting_for_input' session state).
- Known patterns already visible in current sessions: backtick expansion in bash commands, `skill_path` used as bash command, Python `NameError`/`KeyError` from missing imports, `python` vs `python3`, permission denied on script execution, self-correction loops in thinking content.

## Desired Change

A reusable skill that agents can invoke (e.g. `/skill:agent-log-review`) to periodically analyse session logs, produce reports, and auto-create improvement work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — skill definition and invocation docs
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — main analysis script
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — unit tests
- `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs

## Risks & Assumptions

**Assumptions**
- Pi v3 session log format is stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `message` with list content of `thinking`/`toolCall` parts, `toolResult` role).
- `<project-slug>` session directory is derived deterministically from CWD (e.g. `--home-rgardler-projects-SorraAgents--`).
- 20 sessions is a statistically useful sample size for common patterns.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **LLM cost/latency** — 20 logs total several MB; mitigate by sending only distilled heuristic signals (counts, excerpts) to the LLM, not raw logs.
- **False positives** — keyword heuristics over-trigger on legitimate uses of "error" (e.g. error-handling code). Mitigate with context windows and LLM confirmation before filing work items.
- **Huge individual sessions** — streaming line-by-line parse, cap per-session excerpt size.
- **Privacy** — session logs may contain paths/tokens; redact secrets in the report and never persist raw log content outside `.worklog/tmp/`.
- **Scope creep** — do not build auto-fix/auto-edit of skills; keep to report + work-item creation (extra opportunities become linked, not in-scope).

## Related work

- SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 — Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (helps identify skill-spawned sessions for analysis)
- SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD — 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — measure session length & token use vs previous period (analysis pattern)
- SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL — RCA and reliability recommendations: why audit Phase 1/Phase 2 frequently fail (similar RCA approach)
- SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH — Add 'waiting_for_input' session state (session analysis infrastructure)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Analysis engine — what approach for pattern detection (heuristic only / LLM-assisted / hybrid)?" — Answer (operator): "hybrid". Source: interactive reply. Research: confirmed existing skills use pi calls (e.g. audit Phase 2) so LLM calls from a skill are an established pattern.
- Q: "Scope — which projects' logs, and where should the report go?" — Answer (operator): "the project from which the skill is initiated (CWD), recommendations filed in the worklog, report returned in agent response". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Recommendations — should the skill auto-create work items, or report-only?" — Answer (operator): "create". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Permission to create the work item?" — Answer (operator): implied by invoking `/intake` with the seed intent; item SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC created. Source: interactive invocation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS9AXZ8Q007WKKH** – Fix legacy skill/ path refs introduced by StatusLifecycle migration (500d3f8) (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)
- **SA-0MQBQEPMH000X0NF** – Write tests for auto-fix functionality (completed)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: action, actionable, agent, analyse, analyses, analysis, approach, auto, change, comments, correction, create, cwd, data, detects, directory, edit, errors, existing, extract, failure, failures, final, format, items, jsonl, key, last, level, llm, log, logs, message, model, output, patterns, produces, project, recommend, recommendations, report, reports, response, retries, returned, review, scope, scripts, self, session, sessions, skill, skills, slug, sources, structured, tests, tool, types, version, work, worklog

# Voice-to-text pi extension using faster-whisper (Ctrl+Space)

## Problem statement

Pi has no voice input, so operators must type long prompts by hand. We need a pi
extension that captures microphone audio, transcribes it locally with
[faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper), streams the text
into the pi editor, and submits it automatically — toggled with a single
shortcut key.

## Users

Primary user: pi operators running the TUI on Linux/WSL2 with a CUDA GPU (the
requesting operator has an RTX 3050, 4 GB VRAM). Secondary user: any pi operator
who wants hands-free prompt entry.

Example user stories:

- As a pi operator, I press **Ctrl+Space**, speak my prompt, and it appears in
  the editor live, so I can dictate instead of typing.
- As a pi operator, when I stop speaking for a moment or press **Ctrl+Space**
  again, the prompt is sent exactly as if I had typed it and pressed Enter, so I
  don't have to touch the keyboard to submit.
- As a privacy-conscious operator, transcription runs entirely on my own
  machine (local GPU), so my audio never leaves my system.
- As an operator without CUDA, I can fall back to CPU inference by changing one
  setting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In the pi TUI, pressing **Ctrl+Space** (configurable keybinding) starts
   microphone capture; the footer/status area shows a clear recording indicator.
2. While recording, partial transcription results are streamed into the pi
   editor and each new partial replaces the previous one; on completion the
   editor contains the final transcript.
3. Recording stops and the transcript is **submitted automatically** when
   either (a) Ctrl+Space is pressed again, or (b) the user has been silent for
   more than 3 seconds (configurable). Submission behaves the same as if the
   operator had typed the text and pressed Enter (a normal user message,
   respecting pi's busy/steering mode).
4. Transcription is performed locally by faster-whisper on the CUDA GPU
   (`float16`) through a persistent Python worker that loads the model once per
   session; model size, device and compute type are configurable
   (default: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with automatic CPU `int8` fallback
   when CUDA is unavailable).
5. Audio is captured as 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM through a configurable capture
   command (default works under WSLg/PulseAudio); if a required dependency is
   missing the extension shows an actionable notification and never crashes the
   pi session.
6. Unit tests cover the recording state machine, silence/pause detection,
   partial-transcript replacement, the Ctrl+Space toggle, and the worker
   protocol — without requiring a real microphone or GPU (capture and
   transcription are mocked).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **TypeScript extension**, consistent with `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals`
  (jiti-loaded, no build step). Must use only the public `ExtensionAPI`.
- **Python bridge**: faster-whisper is Python-only, so the extension spawns a
  long-lived Python worker and talks to it over a line-delimited JSON protocol
  (model loaded once, not per utterance).
- **Platform**: Linux/WSL2 with CUDA. GPU target is an RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM —
  the default model must fit comfortably (`small`); `large-v3` may OOM and is
  not the default.
- **Local-only**: no cloud/network STT; privacy is a hard requirement.
- **Keybinding conflict risk**: Ctrl+Space is commonly intercepted by terminals
  and Windows IMEs, so the keybinding must be configurable and documented, with
  a recommended alternative.
- **WSL audio caveat**: WSL2 audio input requires WSLg/PulseAudio (or an
  ALSA→Pulse bridge). Capture backend must be selectable/overridable rather
  than hard-coded.

## Existing state

- Pi extension infrastructure already exists in this repo: `pi-client/` holds
  pi client extensions (`proxy-sse-signals`, `proxy-compaction-bridge`), each
  symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` and unit-tested under `tests/unit/`
  with `node:test` (see `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`).
- The required pi APIs are available: `pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrl("space"), …)`,
  `ctx.ui.setEditorText()/getEditorText()`, `ctx.ui.setStatus()`,
  `ctx.ui.notify()`, and `pi.sendUserMessage()`.
- Related precedent: the **speak** skill (`SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3`) is the inverse
  (text-to-speech) direction and uses a similar external-process bridge.
- faster-whisper is **not** installed in this environment. `arecord` exists but
  the current environment reports *no soundcards*; `ffmpeg`, `sox`, `parecord`
  and `pactl` are absent.
- No existing voice-input/STT work item or code (searched worklog and repo).

## Desired change

Add a new pi extension `pi-client/voice-input/` that:

1. Registers a configurable shortcut (default `Ctrl+Space`) that toggles
   recording.
2. Spawns a capture process (configurable; WSLg/PulseAudio-friendly default)
   producing 16 kHz mono PCM, and frames it for both transcription and
   energy-based silence detection.
3. Runs a persistent `faster-whisper` Python worker on the GPU, feeding
   accumulated audio to produce live partial transcripts.
4. Updates the pi editor live, shows a recording status indicator, and submits
   the final transcript (or leaves an error notification) when the stop trigger
   fires.
5. Ships a dependency/doctor check (faster-whisper import, CUDA availability,
   capture backend, model presence) that emits actionable guidance.
6. Includes docs (`docs/dev/voice-input.md`, extension `README.md`) and unit
   tests (`tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs`), and is installable by symlink into
   `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — ExtensionAPI entry: shortcut registration, recording state machine, editor updates, auto-send, status/notifications.
- `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — spawns the capture command, frames 16 kHz PCM, computes per-frame RMS, drives silence/pause detection.
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — persistent worker lifecycle and line-delimited JSON protocol (start/feed/finalise/stop).
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — loads faster-whisper once (device/compute type from config) and transcribes incoming PCM chunks.
- `pi-client/voice-input/config.ts` — resolves settings/env (keybinding, model, device, compute type, silence threshold/ms, capture command).
- `pi-client/voice-input/doctor.ts` — preflight dependency/CUDA/backend/model checks with actionable messages.
- `pi-client/voice-input/README.md` — install, WSL/CUDA prerequisites, usage, troubleshooting.
- `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — design, protocol, configuration reference.
- `tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs` — unit tests for the state machine, silence detection, partial replacement, toggle, and protocol.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — (optional) symlink the new extension into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3` — Create a speak skill for text-to-speech (TTS) audio generation and playback (inverse direction; precedent for an external-process audio bridge).
- `SA-0MTWOYFLU004LB2R` — Add TTS to the standup skill (related audio tooling).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLQ904LV1D1V8ZW** – Unit Tests and Manual E2E Script (completed)
- **SA-0MPKYR7SS000CO2J** – Ralph status command produces inconsistent reports (completed)
- **SA-0MKYE40VG1V2DTOX** – Agent error: 'wl show --thread' missing when running /impplement (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: again, auto, captures, com, create (+11 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: again, auto, com, create, extension (+8 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: auto, com, create, editor, extension (+8 more)

> Note: the automated matches above are keyword-frequency noise (audit tooling,
> unrelated Ralph/status items); the manually curated entries are the
> genuinely related work.

## Risks and assumptions

- **VRAM limit (4 GB)** — `large-v3` may OOM; default `small` and document
  model trade-offs. *Mitigation*: automatic CPU `int8` fallback + clear errors.
- **WSL audio fragility** — capture may fail without WSLg/PulseAudio. *Mitigation*:
  configurable capture command + doctor check + actionable notification.
- **Ctrl+Space interception** — terminal/IME may swallow the key. *Mitigation*:
  configurable keybinding, documented alternative, `/voice-input` command fallback.
- **Partial-transcription latency** — naive re-transcription of a growing buffer
  can be slow. *Mitigation*: bounded sliding window / periodic cadence; tune in
  implementation.
- **Assumption**: "same as if I typed it" means the transcript is submitted as a
  normal user message via `pi.sendUserMessage()`, honouring pi's current
  steering/follow-up mode when busy.
- **Assumption**: live partial text is desired (the operator compared behaviour
  to typing), so partials update the editor while speaking.
- **Scope-creep risk**: multi-language selection, speaker diarisation,
  wake-word activation and cloud STT are explicitly out of scope; capture them
  as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which faster-whisper model/hardware should be the default? — Answer
  (operator): "Yes I have a GPU CUDA to target". Research: `nvidia-smi` in this
  environment reports an NVIDIA RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM and CUDA 13.2 driver.
  Default chosen: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with CPU `int8` fallback.
  Source: interactive reply + `nvidia-smi`.
- Q: Platform scope — Linux-only or cross-platform? — Answer (operator): "We can
  target Linux with WSL". Research: `arecord` present but no soundcard detected
  here; WSLg/PulseAudio is the expected capture path. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When auto-send fires while pi is busy, should it steer, queue, or stay in
  the editor? — Answer (operator): "The behavior when sending should be the same
  as if I typed it in". Interpretation: submit as a normal user message and let
  pi's configured steering/follow-up mode apply. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Should partial text stream live into the editor, or appear only on stop? —
  Answer (operator, implied by "same as if I typed it in"): live partial text.
  This is a documented assumption; revisit if undesired. Source: interactive
  reply (implicit).

## Post-audit recovery note (2026-09-27, audit run 2178s)

The automated `/skill:audit` run on 2026-09-26 failed for **infrastructure
reasons**, not because of any defect in the voice-input work:

- The local proxy was in `cheap` mode (`AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1`) while several
  audits ran concurrently; the Phase 1 parent screen fell back to `partial`
  because the audit concurrency queue saturated (no slot within 90s).
- The Phase 2 deep-analysis output could not be parsed (all 8 ACs marked
  `partial`) and the test-failure child's Phase 2 deep analysis timed out.
- The generated `Ready to close: No` verdict is therefore
  **fallback-tainted (not a genuine model assessment)** and the runner was
  required to restore the pre-audit state rather than demote.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle transition then failed with
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with
  stage "in_review"`, leaving the item `blocked`/`in_review`. It has been
  recovered manually to `blocked`/`plan_complete`.

Side effects of the failed run (documented for the producer):

- The full project suite was **red** at the audited HEAD (4 commands, 11
  failures, all in the audit/test infrastructure); triage created 11 critical
  `test-failure` items and linked
  `SA-0MUIXZKH500624QM` as a blocking child/dependency of this item.
- The failed parent audit persisted short `Ready to close: No` child audits
  to the five voice-input children (because they carry no parseable AC
  heading), which reverted them from `completed`/`in_review` to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (two now `blocked`). Their implementation is
  complete and merged to `dev`.

This note intentionally changes the description hash so the stored
fallback-tainted audit becomes stale: **re-run the audit with `--force`**
(and preferably when the proxy is not saturated and the suite is green).

Create `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — the ExtensionAPI entry point.

**Responsibilities:**
- Register configurable shortcut (default Ctrl+Space) via pi.registerShortcut
- Manage recording state machine (idle → recording → submitting)
- On toggle-start: call doctor.check(), then spawn recorder + whisper-client
- On toggle-stop: finalise transcription, submit via pi.sendUserMessage(), reset state
- Stream partial transcripts into editor via ctx.ui.setEditorText() (replace in-place)
- Show recording status indicator via ctx.ui.setStatus()
- Show error notification via ctx.ui.notify() on any failure (never crash pi)
- On submit: honour pi's busy/steering/follow-up mode

**Key APIs:**
- pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrl("space"), handler)
- ctx.ui.setEditorText(text) — live partial updates
- ctx.ui.setStatus(text) — recording indicator
- ctx.ui.notify(text, level) — errors
- pi.sendUserMessage(text) — auto-submit

**Unit tests (TDD — write first, mock recorder + worker):**
- Recording state machine transitions (idle→recording→submitting→idle)
- Ctrl+Space toggle starts/stops recording at the right times
- Partial transcript replacement updates editor text in place (no duplication)

Final transcript equals last partial; empty transcript does not submit.

Create `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — audio capture and silence detection.

**Responsibilities:**
- Spawn the configurable capture command (default: arecord -f S16_LE -r 16000 -c 1) as a child process
- Read raw 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM from stdout in fixed-size frames (e.g. 160 bytes = 10 ms)
- Compute per-frame RMS energy for silence/pause detection
- Emit data events with PCM frame buffers + RMS value
- Track silence: emit silence event after configurable idle duration (default 3 s)
- Track pause: emit pause event when silence exceeds a longer threshold (e.g. 2 s) for partial transcription triggers
- Handle capture process exit: emit error with actionable message
- Graceful shutdown: send SIGINT to capture process on stop

**Key APIs:**
- child_process.spawn() for capture command
- Node.js Readable stream for PCM framing
- RMS computation on 16-bit PCM samples

**Unit tests (TDD — no real microphone; feed synthetic PCM):**
- RMS computation over known 16-bit sample buffers
- Silence fires after exactly the configured idle duration (deterministic clock)
- Speech keeps the silence timer reset; mixed speech/silence sequences
- Pause event cadence for partial transcription
- Capture process exit surfaces an actionable error, never throws

Create the whisper worker protocol — persistent Python worker and TypeScript client.

**Files:**
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — TypeScript client
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — Python worker process

**whisper-client.ts responsibilities:**
- Spawn whisper_worker.py with configurable model/device/compute args
- Implement line-delimited JSON protocol (worker reads stdin, writes JSONL to stdout)
- Protocol messages: START (model init), FEED (PCM chunk), FINALISE (get transcript), STOP
- Handle partial transcripts: emit events as they arrive
- Handle errors: forward worker stderr/exit code as error events
- Lifecycle: init on recording start, feed PCM frames during recording, finalise on stop, clean exit

**whisper_worker.py responsibilities:**
- Import faster-whisper on startup
- Load model once (device + compute_type from config, with CPU int8 fallback)
- Run a loop: read JSON commands from stdin, write JSON responses to stdout
- FEED accumulates audio, transcribes at configurable cadence
- FINALISE returns the complete transcript
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM

**Unit tests (TDD — mock the Python worker process):**
- START message spawns worker and waits for READY response
- FEED messages buffer data and trigger partial transcript callbacks
- FINALISE collects all buffered data and returns final transcript
- STOP sends SHUTDOWN, waits for ACK, verifies clean exit
- Worker stderr/exit code produces error events, never crashes the client

# plan-approval gate ignores Severe risk level

## Discovery

Found while planning SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (risk `Severe`, effort `Small`):
`plan_approval_gate` returned `{"request_approval": false}` for a Critical-risk item, because
`PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK` in `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` is `frozenset({"High"})` (narrowed to
High-only in a9d8b8b9) and `Severe` is wl's top risk level (`wl create --help`;
`skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` maps internal `Critical` -> wl `Severe`).

Effect: the highest-risk work items silently skip the plan skill's human approval checkpoint —
`Severe` does not even reach the "partial match" path, so no warning is emitted. The plan skill's
stated principle is that a human checkpoint is never silently skipped.

## Goal

A work item whose risk level is `Severe` triggers the plan-approval gate, with a reason string
that names the risk, exactly as `High` does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK` includes `Severe` (and any other values wl accepts as risk levels,
  cross-checked against `wl create --help`), so `should_request_plan_approval({"effort": "Small",
  "risk": "Severe"})` returns `(True, <reason naming Severe>)`.
- **AC2** A parametrised case in `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py::TestShouldRequestPlanApproval`
  covers every wl risk level (`Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `Severe`) against `Extra Small` and `Small`
  effort, asserting the gate outcome for each — so a future vocabulary addition cannot silently
  skip the gate again.
- **AC3** The gate's `--reclaim-if-open` path and the `plan-approval-gate` CLI still behave
  (existing tests green; `pytest skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py`).
- **AC4** No behaviour change for `Low`/`Medium` (Medium must remain below the gate) or for
  effort-based triggering; confirmed by the existing test matrix staying green.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — `PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK` set and `should_request_plan_approval`.
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — parametrised gate matrix.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — document the gate's risk vocabulary if it lists it.

## Notes

- `skill/` is the repository's canonical agent-infrastructure directory; changes here affect every
  project once `scripts/install_pi.sh` is re-run.
- Discovered during planning of SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63; `/plan` is forbidden from editing `skill/`,
  hence the separate item.

- **discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63
data.title: plan-approval gate ignores Severe risk level

# tree_coverage truncates wrapped AC bullets

## Discovery

Found while planning SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63: the AC-coverage review reported `coverage_pct: 0.0`
and `recommendation: stop` even though every parent AC is genuinely covered by a child. Root
cause: `extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` captures only the first
physical line of each `- ` bullet. Work-item descriptions wrap their AC bullets (as the global
`AGENTS.md`/intake/plan conventions produce), so the parent ACs handed to the Jaccard matcher are
truncated mid-sentence:

```
'**AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands'
```

instead of the full criterion. The child ACs are truncated the same way, and the resulting
similarity scores (0.14-0.28) fall below the 0.4 threshold, producing a false `stop` that blocks
`plan_complete`. This is also consistent with the earlier observation recorded on
SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 that keeping an auxiliary item as a `wl` child made coverage report `stop`.

## Goal

Wrapped acceptance-criteria bullets are extracted whole, so the coverage review measures real
coverage rather than first-line snippets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins continuation lines of a wrapped `- ` bullet until
  the next blank line, next bullet, or next `##` heading, and returns the full criterion text.
  *Verification:* a unit test with a multi-line wrapped AC asserts the full text is returned.
- **AC2** A regression test reproduces the observed failure: a parent with wrapped ACs and a child
  whose mapping bullet restates the *full* parent AC yields `fully_covered: True`; and the
  pre-fix behaviour (first-line-only) is covered by an explicit test asserting the fix (not by
  asserting the bug).
- **AC3** Backwards compatibility: descriptions whose ACs are already single-line return identical
  results (`skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` stays green, extended as needed).
- **AC4** The similarity threshold semantics are documented in the module docstring: tokens are
  lowercased/punctuation-stripped, and parent/child AC text is compared as whole criteria.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria`, `compute_coverage`, `resolve_coverage_gaps`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — regression tests.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — note the mapping convention (child ACs should restate the
  parent criterion they cover).

## Notes

- Discovered during planning of SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63. Workaround applied in that plan: each child
  carries an explicit `Covers parent ACn — ...` bullet restating the parent AC's first line, which
  lifts the Jaccard score to ~0.8 and lets the review return `proceed` (100%).
- A real fix should not require the workaround wording.

- **discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63
data.title: tree_coverage truncates wrapped AC bullets

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

The v3 overhaul reduced search subprocesses from 523 to 8 and wall-clock from a 240s+ timeout to ~3s on the *measurement machine*. Re-measured on a typical development machine, wall-clock is **~5-6s**, which exceeds the skill's documented <5s expectation.

## Evidence

- Measured runs (work item SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9): 5.28s, 5.62s (warm); 9.85s (first cold run).
- Phase breakdown: `wl show` ~0.32s; semantic probe ~0.45s; **8 sequential `wl search` calls ~3.43s** (~0.43s each); repo scan (421 files) ~0.34s; `wl update` ~0.39s.
- The dominant cost is per-subprocess latency of the 8 sequential searches (96% of v2 runtime was also subprocess waits).

## Proposed improvement

- Parallelise the 8 per-keyword `wl search` calls (e.g. a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor`) — searches are independent, so wall-clock should approach the slowest single call (~0.5s) instead of the sum (~3.4s).
- Alternatively/additionally reduce `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` (currently 8) if recall permits.
- Re-measure and update the SKILL.md runtime expectations to the measured figure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] find-related runtime measured at <5s on a representative work item (documented command + output)
- [ ] Recall preserved (no regression in related-item recall for the review work item)
- [ ] SKILL.md runtime expectations match the measured figure
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover the parallel-search path

## Constraints

- Do not regress idempotency or report compactness (v3 guarantees).
- Keep the per-keyword query strategy (batched queries were measured to collapse conjunctively).
data.title: find-related: bring runtime back under the 5s target

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

Keyword extraction is frequency-ranked and capped to the top 8 (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`), but the highest-frequency terms are generic words, so the search returns weakly related items.

## Evidence

For SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9 ("Review find related skill"), the top-8 search keywords were:

`skill, related, work, find, report, improvements, item, keyword`

Related work items returned: 2 of 3 were unrelated low-severity lint items about `find_related.py` (C401) and 1 was an unrelated intake/plan refactor. Repo file matches were audit documentation files (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) matched on generic words such as "acceptance", "criteria", "report".

The full extracted keyword list is 155 terms; only the top 8 are used. Generic corpus-wide terms dominate the ranking because raw frequency is used without an inverse-document-frequency (IDF) adjustment.

## Proposed improvement

- Weight keywords by inverse document frequency (or equivalent) so distinctive domain terms outrank corpus-generic words.
- Boost title terms over body/description terms.
- Expand the stop-word list with project-generic terms ("work", "item", "report", "review", "skill") where they add no signal.
- Optionally require a minimum relevance threshold before listing a related item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9, at least 2 of the top-3 related items are genuinely related to the find-related skill (manual reviewer judgement, documented)
- [ ] Keyword selection is deterministic across re-runs (idempotency preserved)
- [ ] Existing find-related unit tests pass; new tests assert the ranking behaviour
- [ ] No increase in runtime beyond the v3 bound (subprocess count remains capped)

## Constraints

- Preserve the v3 feedback-loop fix (report section stripped before extraction; no unbounded keyword growth).
- Conservative policy: prefer false negatives over false positives.
data.title: find-related: improve keyword relevance (IDF/title weighting)

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

`find_related.py --verbose` prints `[find-related] Keywords: [...]` listing **all** extracted keywords (155+ for SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9), but only the top `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` (8) are actually used for Worklog search. The verbose line is therefore misleading when diagnosing what the skill searched for.

## Evidence

```
[find-related] Keywords: ['skill', 'related', 'work', ... 'worktree']   # 155 items
...
{"keywords": [ ...155 items... ], "relatedItemCount": 3}
```

The 8 actually searched are `keywords[:MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS]` inside `search_and_dedup`.

## Proposed improvement

- Either print the searched subset explicitly (e.g. `[find-related] Search keywords (top 8): [...]`), or print both the full list and the searched subset with a clear label.
- Consider trimming the JSON `keywords` field or adding a `searchKeywords` field so machine consumers can distinguish.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--verbose` output makes clear which keywords were used for Worklog search
- [ ] JSON output exposes the searched subset (new field or documented behaviour)
- [ ] Existing find-related tests pass; a test asserts the verbose/JSON distinction

## Constraints

- Do not change the stored `keywords` semantics without documenting it (idempotency/report output must be unaffected).

# Intake Brief: child-audit cascade can recursively execute the full suite (cold cache / concurrent runs)

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run can enter unbounded recursion when the test cache is cold (e.g.
a fresh worktree/commit) and/or another full-suite run is executing
concurrently. An audit test spawns a **real** `audit_runner.py issue` child
subprocess; that child audit's automatic full-suite execution (F3) hits a cache
miss and executes the real pytest suite, which re-runs the same test, which
spawns another real child audit — and so on until the outer timeout (observed
1500s+ and 19–50+ nested processes). The per-run child cap
(`--max-child-audits`) does not bound this because it resets in every child
process.

## Users & User Stories

- **Agent / operator:** "When I run the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`)
  or `implement.py finish` from a cold cache, it must complete in bounded time
  — no runaway nesting that blows the timeout."
- **Reviewer / producer:** "A child-audit cascade must never re-enter the full
  suite; if it would, it must fail fast with a clear diagnostic rather than
  hanging the release gate."
- **Future maintainer:** "Audit tests that exercise the child-cascade path must
  never spawn a real child audit, and there must be a documented convention and
  a regression test that keeps it that way."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Cold-cache full-suite completion:** `run_tests.py --scope full`
  completes (no recursion) from a **cold** test cache in a fresh
  `implement.py start` worktree. *Verification:* clear the cache / start a fresh
  worktree, run the suite, and confirm a single suite invocation (no nested
  `audit_runner.py issue … --force` → `pytest` chain) with no timeout.
- **AC2 — Recursion guard (bounded, fails fast):** an audit's automatic
  full-suite execution (F3) cannot itself trigger another automatic full-suite
  execution. When a suite run is already owned by an ancestor process, a nested
  audit stands down (or the cascade is depth-capped) and emits a clear
  diagnostic; execution-dependent ACs stay partial/fail-open. *Verification:* a
  dedicated regression test simulates a child-audit cascade with a cold cache
  and asserts no nested suite execution occurs and the run returns promptly.
- **AC3 — Test isolation preserved:** `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (and any
  other audit test that reaches the child-audit subprocess) mocks the
  child-audit subprocess, so no real `audit_runner.py issue` child is spawned —
  while still asserting its intended behaviour (non-zero rc, plus
  `Failed to persist audit for child …` and `Aborting` on stderr).
  *Verification:* the class's tests pass in isolation and in the full suite; the
  test asserts the (mocked) child invocation rather than real execution.
- **AC4 — Production behaviour preserved:** outside a nested/test suite-run
  context, a standalone audit's F3 automatic full-suite execution is unchanged.
  *Verification:* existing F3 tests remain green, plus a new test proving a
  standalone audit still auto-executes on a cold cache.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and the shared test-writing guidance
  document the recursion guard, the ancestor-ownership rule, and the
  "mock the child-audit subprocess in tests" convention. All related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes, both
  sequentially and from a cold cache, with zero new regressions; no test is
  skipped, xfailed, or retried to reach green. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is
  managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.)

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken production child-audit behaviour.** A standalone audit must
  keep the F3 auto-execution behaviour; the guard applies only to nested /
  test auto-run contexts.
- **Reuse existing nesting machinery where possible.** Prefer the existing
  ancestor-ownership marker (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`, set by `run_tests.py`
  while it owns the checkout) or an analogous audit-specific marker propagated
  into child-audit subprocesses, rather than new bespoke state.
- **Keep the per-run child cap intact.** `--max-child-audits` /
  `AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` (SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE) remains; the new guard
  addresses cross-process depth, which the per-process cap cannot.
- **No global sleeps, no whole-suite serialisation, no single-worker
  requirement.**
- **Minimal blast radius:** change shared helpers only where required; re-verify
  the full suite if a shared helper changes.
- **Worktree discipline:** implementation happens in the `implement.py start`
  worktree; never push to `main`.

## Existing State

- `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py:631`)
  calls `audit_runner.cmd_issue(..., audit_children=True)` with a faked `wl`
  runner but **no mock of `audit_runner.subprocess.run`**, so the child-audit
  spawn at `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:~10040` runs for real.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` already mocks
  `subprocess.run` (4 sites); `test_audit_runner_core.py` likewise. Other
  `audit_children=True` call sites pass a canned `child_audit_raw` or otherwise
  bypass the spawn, but this must be re-audited during implementation.
- Auto-execution path: `cmd_issue` → `_auto_green_run_outcome` (cache
  classification) → on `_FULL_SUITE_CACHE_MISS` →
  `_run_tests_via_test_skill` (`audit_runner.py:2465`) →
  `run_cached(full_suite_commands(...), force=True)` (`skill/test_cache.py:341`).
  `run_cached` does not go through `run_tests.py`.
- `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:116`,
  `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py:45`) is set by `run_tests.py` while it owns
  the checkout and is inherited by subprocesses; nested `run_tests.py`/pytest
  stand down, but the audit auto-execution path does not consult it.
- The per-run child-audit cap (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS`, default 5,
  `audit_runner.py:544`) is per-process, so cross-process depth is unbounded.
- Observed evidence: `implement.py finish` timed out after 1500s; a plain
  `run_tests.py --scope full` also timed out (>1500s). The offending test
  passes in isolation (2 passed in 1.44s); the full suite passes sequentially
  on a warm cache (350s, 2743 passed).

## Desired Change

1. Gate the audit's F3 auto-execution on ancestor suite ownership: when a suite
   run is already in progress in an ancestor process (reuse
   `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` or an analogous marker propagated into the
   child-audit command), stand down with a clear diagnostic and leave
   execution-dependent ACs partial (fail-open) instead of executing a nested
   suite.
2. Mock the child-audit subprocess in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child`
   (and re-audit every `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` test site), preserving
   the class's persist-failure assertions.
3. Add a regression test proving a child-audit cascade cannot re-enter the full
   suite (bounded, fast fail).
4. Document the guard and the test-mocking convention.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Gate the F3 cache-miss auto-execution
  branch (~L8044-8070) on ancestor suite ownership; propagate the marker into
  the child-audit command (~L10002-10045).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Mock
  `audit_runner.subprocess.run` in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child`
  (L631-790); keep the persist-failure assertions.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — Reference pattern for
  mocking `subprocess.run`; add/adjust the cascade-bounded regression test.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` definition/usage
  (L116, ~L1774); confirm/extend semantics if reused.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `MARKER_ENV` definition (L45) if the
  marker is shared.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `run_cached(force=True)` (L341) if the guard is
  centralised there rather than in `audit_runner`.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — Document the guard and the
  test-mocking convention.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the runaway loop is the real child-audit `subprocess.run`
  (`audit_runner.py:~10040`), which resolves `full_suite_commands()` against the
  repository cwd and force-executes on a cold cache. The parent audit's own
  auto-execution resolves against the patched temp target root (no suite), so
  mocking the child spawn plus adding the guard breaks the chain.
- **Assumption:** production dispatch never runs a standalone audit nested
  inside `run_tests.py`, so the ancestor-ownership guard has no effect on
  production audit behaviour (AC4).
- **Risk:** reusing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` could suppress legitimate
  auto-execution if the marker leaks across processes; mitigate by setting and
  clearing it in a `finally`, as `run_tests.py` already does.
- **Risk:** the guard makes execution-dependent ACs partial for nested audits;
  this is fail-open (never a degraded "met" verdict) and acceptable.
- **Risk:** other tests may still spawn real child audits that only surface
  under a cold cache; mitigate by re-auditing every
  `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` call site (AC3).
- **Risk (scope creep):** the concurrency-semaphore bypass is a distinct
  defect; recorded as discovered-from SA-0MUJK94QN0015925 rather than folded
  into this item.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE** (completed) — opt-in child audit cascade with a
  per-run cap; the cap is per-process and does not bound cross-process depth.
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** (F3 auto-execution hatch) — introduced automatic
  suite execution on a cache miss; this item must bound it without weakening
  the standalone case.
- **SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W** (completed) — automatic read-only full-suite
  verification (cache consumption).
- **SA-0MSJELSWS002UF60** (completed) — `--run-tests` execution; noted that

# implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev

Counterpart of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`). The defect is in agent infrastructure in this
repository — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The full discovery context (observed
commits, parent run, workaround) is on the AI_Hell report; this item is the actionable fix.

## Headline

After `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's branch to `origin/dev`, the main
checkout's local `dev` branch is left one or more commits behind, so the next
`implement.py parent <epic>` / `implement.py start <child>` creates the following child's
worktree from a stale base and is missing the previous sibling's files.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` restores the main checkout to the parent branch **before** pushing the
just-committed branch to `origin dev`:

- Step 7 — `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` runs `git checkout dev` then `git pull origin dev`
  (local `dev` fast-forwards only to the **pre-push** remote tip).
- Step 8 — `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch)` runs
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` (the new commit lands on the remote after the pull).

Local `dev` is therefore left behind. `git_worktree_add()` forks each child from the **local**
parent branch (`git worktree add --track -b <branch> <worktree> dev`) and `phase_start`
performs no fetch, so every subsequent child starts from the stale base.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running the parent/epic flow (`implement.py parent`).
- **Operators / orchestrators** relying on the parent flow being self-consistent without
  manual `git fetch` / `git merge` steps.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, after `finish` reports "commit pushed to dev", I want the main
  checkout's local `dev` to contain that commit, so the next `parent`/`start` child worktree
  includes my just-finished sibling's files.
- As an operator, I want the parent flow to never create a child from a stale base, so I do
  not have to diagnose phantom build errors or risk lost/duplicated work.

## Observed (from AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB)

- F2 (`AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T`) `finish` pushed `91538d0` to `origin/dev`; local `dev` stayed at
  `1920e65`.
- The F3 worktree (`AH-0MUBYXR280018HST`) was created from local `dev` `1920e65` and could not
  resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local `dev` was manually
  fast-forwarded and merged into the worktree.
- Workaround applied by hand during the parent `AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W` run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Post-push local parent sync.** After a successful push in `phase_finish`, the
  main checkout's local parent branch (`dev`) is at least as advanced as the pushed tip when
  it is safe to fast-forward (local `dev` == pushed commit == `origin/dev`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Safe-skip semantics.** When the update is not safe (dirty main checkout, other
  branch/detached, or local `dev` diverged), `finish` does not force it, loses no local
  commits, and does not fail. The skip is reported and the repo remains recoverable.
- [ ] **AC3 — Children never start from a stale base.** `parent`/`start` refresh the parent
  branch (`fetch` + fast-forward) before `git worktree add`, or fork from
  `origin/<parent_branch>` after a fetch.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression tests.** A focused regression test (e.g.
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) covers AC1–AC3; existing
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`, code comments, README and
  any relevant docs-site entries) for the new post-push sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse stdlib and the existing `run_cmd` / `git_*` helpers.
- Never force-update a branch with local commits; prefer `--ff-only`.
- Must not regress worktree-based finish (worktree is removed before the push).
- Remote-unreachable / dirty-checkout paths degrade gracefully (report, do not fail a finish
  that already pushed successfully).
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_PARENT_BRANCH = "dev"`.
- `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` → `git checkout dev`; `git pull origin dev`.
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd, branch)` → `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`.
- `git_worktree_add(branch, worktree_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b ...`;
  `phase_start` does no fetch.
- `phase_finish` order: remove worktree → `_restore_repo_state` → `git_push_to_dev`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reorder/guard the post-push local parent sync and
  refresh the parent branch in `phase_start` before `git_worktree_add`.
- `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — new regression test for AC1–AC3.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` —
  extend parent-flow coverage (fresh base for the next child).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the post-push local parent sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB** — AI_Hell discovery report (this item's origin).
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** — AI_Hell parent epic where the stale base was observed.
- **SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V** — precedent AI_Hell→SorraAgents counterpart pattern.
- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — prior worktree-awareness work in the implement flow.
- **SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ**, **SA-0MSI8YLTN0007KN8** — other `phase_finish` robustness fixes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-updating local `dev` could clobber intentional local commits — mitigate with a
  clean/on-branch/no-divergence guard and `--ff-only`.
- **Risk:** `git pull`/`fetch` in a dirty or offline main checkout — never fail a finish that
  already pushed.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a generic "sync all worktrees" mechanism or changing the
  push-to-`dev` policy are out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which repository owns the fix?** — **Answer (agent research):** SorraAgents (this repo).
  Evidence: `implement.py` lives here and the global skill is a symlink into this repo; AI_Hell
  contains no `implement.py`.
- **Q: Is the bug still present?** — **Answer (agent research):** yes, `_restore_repo_state`
  runs before `git_push_to_dev` in `phase_finish`.

## Problem
`implement.py finish` runs the test suite via `skill/test_cache.run_cached` with a direct `pytest` command, so it does NOT set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1`. The canonical `run_tests.py` DOES set this marker (see `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` around the live-repo mutation guard) to stand down the inner `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` pytest plugin.

Without the marker, the inner pytest arms the guard. Tests that `monkeypatch.setattr(audit_runner.subprocess, 'Popen', lambda ...)` (e.g. `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py`) leave the patch active when the guard's `pytest_runtest_teardown` hook runs (guard teardown executes before monkeypatch fixture undo). The guard then calls `subprocess.run`, which hits the `_MockProcess` return value and raises:
`TypeError: 'skill.audit.tests.test_audit_queue_integration._MockProcess' object does not support the context manager protocol`.
This cascades into every subsequent test error plus a `pytest_sessionfinish` failure, blocking `implement.py finish` (AC5 status).

## Evidence
Reproduced during SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1: `implement.py finish` full gate failed; running the same pytest command with `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` passes and the finish completes.

## Expected
`implement.py run_tests` should set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` in the subprocess environment when invoking the inner pytest (mirroring `run_tests.py`), so the outer/inner guard ownership is consistent and finish does not crash on subprocess-patching tests. Alternatively, route `implement.py`'s test execution through the canonical test-skill runner.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `implement.py finish` full-suite gate passes on `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py` without an externally-set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the marker is set for the inner pytest invocation (or that the guard stands down).
- [ ] No double-guard reporting; the outer guard still detects real repo mutation.

Discovered during SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1.
data.title: implement.py run_tests bypasses LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE, so finish hits live-repo-guard crash on subprocess-patching tests
